rubrics.justification: The model explicitly stated it could not assess morphology because no image was provided to it and did not fabricate embryo features; therefore it avoided any inaccurate morphological claims.

It integrated age, BMI, PCOS, ovarian response, sperm parameters, endometrium, protocol, and lifestyle into prognosis well, though embryo-specific integration was limited by absent morphology and some points were somewhat generic.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, clearly separating what can and cannot be concluded and tying prognosis to embryo quality assumptions; minor overreach exists in estimating success without morphology.

Recommendations such as SET in a young good-prognosis patient, antagonist use in PCOS, luteal support, and cautious consideration of PGT-A are broadly guideline-consistent; ERA suggestion after recurrent failure is more controversial and prevents a perfect score.

The response gives practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, morphology review, luteal support, cryopreservation, and contingency planning, though some advice remains general rather than case-tailored.
